Arithmetic.Definition: Arithmetic operators perform basic math operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

Assignment.Definition: Assignment operators store a value in a variable. They set or update the variable’s value.

Bitwise.Definition: Bitwise operators perform operations directly on the individual bits of a numeric value. They combine or invert bits using the operators {c:color-teal keyword}&{/c}, {c:color-teal keyword}|{/c}, {c:color-teal keyword}^{/c}, and {c:color-teal keyword}~{/c}.

BooleanLogical.Definition: Boolean logical operators combine or invert true and false values. They are commonly used in conditional expressions.

Comparison.Definition: Comparison operators compare two values and produce a true or false result. They are used in conditions and decision-making.

ExpressionBodyArrow.Definition: Introduces the expression body of a member, indicating that the member's implementation or returned value is provided by the expression that follows.

IndexFromEnd.Definition: The {c:bold}index{/c} operator {c:keyword}^{/c} specifies a position counted from the end of a sequence.

Indirection.Definition: An operator that accesses or produces a value indirectly through a memory address, such as obtaining an address or dereferencing a pointer.

Lambda.Definition: The lambda operator defines an inline function using a concise syntax. It is often used to pass behavior as data.

MemberAccess.Definition: An operator used to access a type member.

NullCoalescing.Definition: The null-coalescing operator provides a fallback value when an expression is null. It helps avoid null reference errors.

NullCoalescingAssignment.Definition: The null-coalescing assignment operator assigns a value only if the target is null. It combines a null check and assignment into one operation.

NullConditionalDot.Definition: The member access part of the null-conditional operator.

NullConditionalQuestion.Definition: The nullable guard part of the null-conditional operator.

NullForgiving.Definition: The null-forgiving operator tells the compiler that a value should be treated as non-null. It does not change runtime behavior.

PatternMatchArrow.Definition: Connects the pattern of a {c:color-purple keyword}switch{/c} expression arm to the value returned when that pattern matches.

RangeSlice.Definition: The {c:keyword}..{/c} operator targets a range of elements in a collection to match or capture.

Shift.Definition: Shift operators move the bits of a numeric value left or right by a specified number of positions. They use the operators {c:color-teal keyword}<<{/c}, {c:color-teal keyword}>>{/c}, and {c:color-teal keyword}>>>{/c}.

TernaryColon.Definition: Marks the expression that is returned when the ternary condition evaluates to {c:bold}false{/c}.

TernaryQuestion.Definition: Marks the expression that is returned when the ternary condition evaluates to {c:bold}true{/c}.
